answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring each identity to dock at a public wharf and cross a sequential bridge of history-bound proofs every epoch. The bridge only advances if the prior wharf attestation is still live and juniper-tied (a non-transferable memory-hard sequential hash chained to that identity's unique key). Splitting into extra heads forces the attacker to fund N independent long-lived sequential chains that cannot be precomputed or parallelized; wall-clock time and exclusive key custody scale linearly with head count while honest agents pay only once.
